content: ---**I INSTABILITY TESTS**---**1 APPREHENSION TEST** Purpose To assess anterior shoulder instability Procedure Abduct the shoulder to 90 flex the elbow to 90 and slowly externally rotate the shoulder Positive Sign Patient becomes apprehensive or fears shoulder dislocation Indicates Anterior glenohumeral instability---**2 JERK TEST** Purpose To assess posterior shoulder instability and posterior labral lesions Procedure Shoulder abducted to 90 and internally rotated Apply axial compression through the elbow while horizontally adducting the arm Positive Sign Painful clunk or jerk Indicates Posterior instability or posterior labral tear---**3 DRAWER TEST** Purpose To assess anterior and posterior glenohumeral instability Procedure Stabilize the scapula and translate the humeral head anteriorly and posteriorly Positive Sign Excessive humeral head movement compared to the opposite side Indicates Shoulder instability---**4 SULCUS SIGN** Purpose To assess inferior glenohumeral instability Procedure Apply downward traction to the relaxed arm Positive Sign Visible sulcus below the acromion Indicates Inferior or multidirectional shoulder instability---**II IMPINGEMENT TESTS**---**1 HAWKINS KENNEDY TEST** Purpose Assess subacromial impingement Procedure Flex shoulder and elbow to 90 and internally rotate the shoulder Positive Sign Pain Indicates Subacromial impingement---**2 NEERS IMPINGEMENT TEST** Purpose Assess subacromial impingement Procedure Stabilize the scapula and passively flex the internally rotated arm Positive Sign Pain Indicates Subacromial impingement---**3 PAINFUL ARC TEST** Purpose Assess shoulder impingement Procedure Ask the patient to actively abduct the shoulder Positive Sign Pain between 60 120 of abduction Indicates Subacromial impingement---**4 EMPTY CAN JOBES TEST** Purpose Assess supraspinatus tendon Procedure Shoulder abducted to 90 in the scapular plane internally rotated thumb down resist downward pressure Positive Sign Pain or weakness Indicates Supraspinatus tendinopathy or tear---**5 DROP ARM TEST** Purpose Assess rotator cuff tear Procedure Passively abduct the arm and ask the patient to slowly lower it Positive Sign Arm drops suddenly or cannot be lowered smoothly Indicates Supraspinatus tear/Rotator cuff tear---**III LABRAL LESION TESTS**---**1 ACTIVE COMPRESSION TEST OBRIEN TEST** Purpose Assess SLAP lesion and AC joint pathology Procedure Shoulder flexed to 90 adducted 10 15 Thumb pointing downward Apply downward resistance Repeat with palm facing upward Positive Sign Pain or clicking that decreases with the palm up position Indicates SLAP lesion or AC joint pathology---**2 KIM TEST** Purpose Assess posteroinferior labral lesion Procedure Shoulder abducted to 90 Apply axial compression with upward and posterior force while elevating the arm diagonally Positive Sign Posterior shoulder pain Indicates Posteroinferior labral tear---**IV SCAPULAR DYSKINESIA TESTS**---**1 SCAPULAR DYSKINESIS TEST** Purpose Assess abnormal scapular movement Procedure Patient performs repeated shoulder flexion and abduction with light weights while the examiner observes scapular motion Positive Sign Scapular winging or asymmetrical movement Indicates Scapular dyskinesia---**2 SCAPULAR LOAD TEST SCAPULAR ASSISTANCE TEST** Purpose Assess the effect of scapular assistance on shoulder movement Procedure Examiner manually assists upward rotation and posterior tilt of the scapula during arm elevation Positive Sign Pain decreases or shoulder movement improves Indicates Scapular dyskinesia---**V MUSCLE PATHOLOGY TESTS**---**1 YERGASONS TEST** Purpose Assess biceps tendon pathology Procedure Patient supinates the forearm against resistance with the elbow flexed to 90 Positive Sign Pain or snapping over the bicipital groove Indicates Biceps tendinitis or transverse humeral ligament injury---**2 SPEEDS TEST** Purpose Assess long head of biceps tendon Procedure Shoulder flexed to 90 elbow extended forearm supinated resist downward pressure Positive Sign Pain in the bicipital groove Indicates Biceps tendinitis or SLAP lesion---**3 LIFT OFF TEST** Purpose Assess Subscapularis muscle Procedure Place the dorsum of the hand on the lower back and ask the patient to lift the hand away Positive Sign Unable to lift the hand or marked weakness Indicates Subscapularis tear or weakness---**4 TEST FOR SUPRASPINATUS** Purpose Assess supraspinatus muscle Procedure Perform the Empty Can Test against resistance Positive Sign Pain or weakness Indicates Supraspinatus pathology---**5 TEST FOR INFRASPINATUS** Purpose Assess infraspinatus muscle Procedure Patient externally rotates the shoulder against resistance with the elbow flexed to 90 Positive Sign Pain or weakness Indicates Infraspinatus tear or weakness---**6 HORNBLOWERS SIGN** Purpose Assess Teres Minor function Procedure Shoulder elevated to 90 in the scapular plane with elbow flexed to 90 Ask the patient to maintain external rotation Positive Sign Unable to maintain the position or external rotation Indicates Teres minor tear or severe rotator cuff pathology
